Implement `applyCatalogCommand(state, command)` and export exactly `{ createCatalogState, applyCatalogCommand }` using CommonJS. `createCatalogState()` returns `{ entries: [] }`. State must be a plain object containing exactly `entries`, an array of records shaped exactly `{ id, title, quantity }`, with non-empty string IDs and titles and nonnegative integer quantities; IDs must be unique. Commands contain an `actor` shaped exactly `{ id, role }`, where both are non-empty strings and role is either `'viewer'` or `'editor'`. Supported commands are `{ type: 'ADD', actor, entry }`, `{ type: 'CHANGE', actor, id, changes }`, and `{ type: 'REMOVE', actor, id }`. `entry` must contain exactly `id`, `title`, and `quantity`. `changes` must be a non-empty plain object containing only `title` and/or `quantity`, with the same value constraints. Only editors may execute commands; viewers cause `Error('Forbidden')`. Duplicate ADD IDs cause `Error('Duplicate id')`; missing CHANGE or REMOVE IDs cause `Error('Entry not found')`. ADD appends, CHANGE preserves position, and REMOVE preserves relative order. Return a new state with fresh copies of every entry and retain no mutable aliases. Malformed or extra fields throw `TypeError`; authorization and validation failures must not mutate state.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
